<hong> and <muak> written as one word: come out to meet or welcome the speaker or those with the speaker
<hongmu>, see us, with the negative <kei>, written as one word: does not see us

<hong>, marking an action toward the speaker, and the preverbal particle <na>, written as one word before a verb, mostly in requests: {hongna maisak in} is please forgive me, {hongna telsiam un} is please understand us
<hong> with <nawk>, strike against, written as one word: come upon and strike us, said of a storm, a disease or an army
<hongnawk> and <ding> written as one word: will come and strike, said of a storm
<hong> and <nei> written as one word: have or hold toward the speaker or the public, as a talk, a meeting or a feeling
<hong> and <neih> written as one word: hold a prayer or a meeting for or with the speaker's side, as in {thungetna hongneih pih}, or come to have something
<hong> and <neihsak> written as one word: hold a prayer or the like on behalf of the speaker and his side
<hong> and <neisak> written as one word: make us or you have a thing, such as a value or a desire
<hong> and <ngah> written as one word: come to receive or win something, with the action seen as coming toward the speaker or his people
<hong> and <ngahkhiat> written as one word: come to obtain or win a thing, such as an office
<hong> and <ngai>, miss, written as one word: miss or long for a person or a place
<hong> and <ngak> written as one word: wait for you or for us
<hong> and <ngen> written as one word: ask for something, toward the speaker or as a plain statement; {thu hongngen} is pray
